summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-M4 admits no external crate. academic-non-delegable links academic-domain, academic-proposal and thiserror as product edges, and academic-audit, academic-consent, academic-deletion, academic-domain, academic-knowledge-state, academic-policy, academic-proposal, academic-record, academic-retention, academic-student-voice and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: every workspace product edge is a path package this repository already builds, and thiserror was admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-non-delegable is the P2-M4 boundary: the compiled non-delegable set and the command layer that refuses MODEL_RUN, IMPORTER and DETERMINISTIC_ENGINE for it. It owns Action, which is closed over section 27.1's ten candidate-generation rows and the execution plan's six non-delegable actions and classifies all sixteen individually so a seventeenth does not compile until it says which side it is on; DecisionEvent, the explicit decision event every non-delegable action requires, which is issued only through P2-M2's UserDecision and binds it to one action and one subject digest; and authorise, the door a command layer calls, which is total over Action and produces either an automatic actor's proposal or one user's decision. It is a separate package from academic-proposal because that crate is the proposal boundary -- what a model proposed and what the system will record -- and this one is the decision boundary, and because the direction of the edge is what keeps the receipt mintable with no action set and the action set impossible without the receipt.

no_second_actor_check_note: The actor refusal is academic_proposal::UserDecision::by, which matches exhaustively over academic-domain's closed Actor enum, so no second actor check is written here and a fifth actor variant stops that crate compiling rather than slipping past a negated list. P2-P2 used the same door for its deletion confirmation, which is what makes this task's compiled constant and that crate's contract one fact rather than two checks that could drift; ai_cannot_confirm_deletion drives that crate's real preview and real confirmation rather than describing them. The four risk tiers are academic_proposal::RiskTier and are section 27.4's own four rows, read through the product edge rather than restated; NonDelegableAction::declared_tier reports which of those rows places each action and reports None for the one section 27 does not name. Sections 27.1 and 27.4 are parsed out of the design document and compared against the action set in both directions, so a count this crate states is the document's rather than one it remembers.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: Actor, ContentDigest and TimestampMillis. The actor is the closed four-variant enum every refusal in this run is expressed over; the digest is the subject a decision event is bound to, so a confirmation of one thing cannot authorise another; and the instant arrives as an argument, because this crate reads no clock. FrozenInputs, InputKey and InputValue are named only by the acceptance suite, for the measurement that a sentence cannot become an engine input.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: P2-M2's UserDecision and RiskTier. UserDecision is issued only for Actor::User by an exhaustive match over a closed enum, so the non-delegable refusal is that crate's door reused; RiskTier is section 27.4's four rows and is what declared_tier answers in, so this crate declares no second tier vocabulary and the_spec_tables_are_this_action_set compares that crate's four tiers against the document's four rows.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-audit: P2-U3's DeterminateVerdict and GraduationOutcome, named by the trybuild case that observes DeterminateVerdict::new is pub(crate). That is the half of graduation_result_cannot_come_from_generation a running test cannot make: no crate outside academic-audit can assemble a verdict from anything at all, generated or otherwise.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-consent: P2-G6's AuthorityGrant, WrittenAuthority, PermittedUse, RetentionTerms and their vocabularies. ai_cannot_attest_permission builds a real grant and observes that AuthorityGrant::record takes no actor, which is how 'the consent layer cannot refuse a model run here' is measured rather than assumed. If that crate ever grows an actor parameter this suite stops compiling, which is the signal that the two layers changed.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-deletion: P2-P2's DeletionTarget, DeletionDryRun, EvidenceCitations, DeletionImpactPreview and DeletionConfirmation, plus the DerivativeIndex and ProtectionRegistry seams the fixture implements. ai_cannot_confirm_deletion drives the real preview and the real confirmation door with every automatic actor and then with the user, so the agreement between this crate's compiled constant and that crate's type is observed rather than described. It stays a dev edge on purpose: a product closure holding the deletion flow would make this crate a shipping-graph dependent of a leaf that P2-Z1 is what will drive.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: Declared a second time for the trybuild reason academic-scenario gives: a compile-fail case compiles against this crate plus this crate's dev-dependencies, and two of the three cases name a TimestampMillis.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-knowledge-state: P2-N2's UserConfirmation and AutomaticLevel. ai_cannot_confirm_mastery drives the real confirmation door with every automatic actor and then observes that no AutomaticLevel maps to MasteryLevel::Fluent, so the one promotion section 13.1 says an AI may never make is still a value the automatic path cannot name.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-policy: P2-G1's PermissionBroker, EgressRule, PolicySnapshot, PermissionRequest and the provider registry. ai_cannot_approve_egress installs two rules identical in all fifteen other fields and different only in actor_id, one naming a user and one naming a model run, and observes the real broker allow both. The allow is the load-bearing half: a pair of denials would have agreed for any reason at all. It stays a dev edge, so no product file here can name a broker, a capability or a staged payload.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: Declared a second time for the same trybuild reason.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-record: P2-U4's RegistrationConfirmation, TermKey, Semester and decimal. ai_cannot_decide_enrollment_or_career builds a real registration confirmation with values a model run could supply and observes it succeed, because RegistrationConfirmation::new takes no actor. That is the measurement behind 'the record layer cannot refuse this', and it is why the refusal for that action is the command layer's.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-retention: P2-K5's DerivativeClass, and nothing else. The DerivativeIndex the deletion fixture implements has that type in its signature and academic-deletion does not re-export it.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-student-voice: P2-L5's EvidenceIndex, and nothing else. academic_deletion::DeletionImpactPreview::of takes one, and building the real preview is what lets the deletion door be driven rather than described.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Three of this task's refusals are absent constructors, and the three cases under crates/non-delegable/tests/compile_fail assert that each is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic -- a decision event written as a struct literal, an authorised proposal written as a struct literal, and a graduation verdict assembled from outside academic-audit.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-non-delegable is the only crate in the workspace that holds the set of actions an AI may not take for the user. Three of the six were already refused by a type -- question resolution in academic-domain, mastery confirmation in academic-knowledge-state, deletion confirmation in academic-deletion -- and three were refused nowhere, because academic_record::RegistrationConfirmation::new and academic_consent::AuthorityGrant::record take no actor and academic_policy's request tuple carries actor_id as an untyped string. A set that lived in any one of those crates would have been that crate's list; a set that lived in six places would have been six lists that could drift. It links academic-proposal because the receipt that proves a user decided is P2-M2's and writing a second one here is exactly the drift this crate exists to prevent; it does not link academic-store, so it holds no canonical writer and adds no migration; and it does not link any of the six crates that own the six actions on the product edge, so no product file in it can name a verdict, a mastery level, a broker or a staged payload.
network_posture: No socket. The crate's link closure carries libc and nothing else, and only through the dev edges: academic-policy's bundled SQLite arrives with the broker the acceptance suite drives. The product closure is academic-domain, academic-proposal and thiserror. The crate itself spells no socket construct, opens no connection, reads no clock and reads no environment variable -- this_crate_reads_no_clock_and_no_environment compares the whole product source for SystemTime, Instant::now, std::env, env::var, option_env!, std::fs and std::process. Nothing here reaches a provider: an egress approval is a decision event carrying an action and a subject digest, and the transmission itself is P2-G2's to stage through P2-G1's broker.
advisory_path: No new advisory surface. Every crate in the closure was admitted by an earlier receipt and is covered by the same cargo-deny and pnpm audit gates the phase 1 receipt names; this task adds no external crate, no build script, no proc macro and no npm package.
